findings.premise: A revision-less receipt appended to the artifact's log has no effect beyond recording the post: it 'moves no revision and no status' (§4 sc4, §5 invariant).
findings.evidence: checkIntegrity (lifecycle.ts:131-140) compares the head only against the LAST log entry: `if (head.contentHash === '' || logTail?.revision === undefined) return { ok: true };`. History.logTail (history.ts:114-117) returns the last entry whatever its kind. lifecycle-service.ts:89 and :250 run this check on approve/complete. A receipt appended after the last content entry therefore turns the head-against-log check (log-ahead-of-head, hash-mismatch) into an automatic pass until the next content write. Every sync can append receipts to an LLD or TASK log. The s7 build-round entries (task-set.ts:368) already do this for TASK heads, but s8 extends it to Story LLDs and to every posted entry, and the LLD does not mention it. [files: src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle.ts, src/workflow/artifact-core/history.ts, src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle-service.ts]
findings.action: State this interaction. Either have checkIntegrity compare against the last log entry that carries a revision (an s3 change, per ruling 3's 'the log's last content entry': coordinate it or file it as an amendment), or keep receipts out of the log tail the check reads.

findings.premise: A failed inbound recording leaves the call repeatable: the since point is the latest tracker-sourced entry's time less a margin, so a comment that failed to record is read again on the next sync (§2.1 'can be repeated', §5 edge 'since point').
findings.evidence: FeedbackService.add stamps an entry with the local clock at recording time (feedback-service.ts:79 `timestamp: (this.deps.now ?? ...)().toISOString()`), not with the comment's creation time. Take comments A (older) and B (newer) read in one sync: if A's add fails transiently (an I/O error on the sidecar append) and B records, the next since point is B's recording time less a margin, which can be later than A's creation, so A is never listed again. A transient failure then becomes a permanent loss. Separately, GitHub's since filters on updated time (port.ts:97 'created or updated at or after it'). An old comment edited after recording is returned again, refused as 'already used with different content' (feedback-service.ts:71) and re-reported as failed on every sync after the edit; §5 does not state this. [files: src/workflow/feedback/feedback-service.ts, src/workflow/tracker/port.ts]
findings.action: Derive the since point from data that survives a partial failure. Options: the earliest comment that failed this pass; the source's comment creation time stored on the entry and compared against the oldest unrecorded comment; or no since at all, using a full listComments with id-based repeats. State that a comment edited after recording is skipped silently, or reported once, rather than failing on every sync.

summary.prose: When the holder starts to implement or validate a Task, or asks for a sync, the comments people wrote on the unit's issue become feedback on the unit's artifact, each recorded once with the tracker user as its author; a comment that starts with a revision or suggestion command is given that kind, and the framework's own posts are never read back. Feedback a person entered here against a unit that has an issue is posted to the issue once and marked as posted. Nothing runs in the background, a later edit or deletion on the tracker is not mirrored, and no new credential is used.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

boundary.internal: Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase D — Tasks and tracker comment sync

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Feedback is recorded through FeedbackService over History; the posting receipt is a revision-less History.appendLog entry; entries carry the Feedback source field the shape already has.
The issue comes from the binding; comments are read with listComments; one additive port method, postComment, is added so a post answers its id.
A Task's feedback is recorded on its TASK head, found from the plan row with taskHeadIdOf.
The unit's artifact is read through ArtifactStore; nothing is written to a head.
Feedback and receipts move no revision and no status.
Entry ids and markers name artifacts by their ArtifactIds form.

errorCases.scenario: The tracker is unreachable or rejects the comment read
errorCases.detection: listComments returns a failed PortResult (unreachable, rejected, missing sign-in)
errorCases.response: The inbound half records nothing and the outbound half still runs only if its own reconciliation read succeeds; the failure is in the result's failed list with its reason, the phase that called the sync carries on
errorCases.userImpact: Implement and validate are never held up by the tracker; the comments are read on the next call

errorCases.scenario: A post succeeds on the tracker but the receipt is not written (the process stops or the append fails)
errorCases.detection: The next sync finds no receipt for the feedback id, lists the issue's comments and finds one carrying the entry's marker
errorCases.response: The receipt is written for that comment and nothing is posted again
errorCases.userImpact: No duplicate comment appears on the issue

errorCases.scenario: A post fails before it reaches the tracker
errorCases.response: No receipt is written, the entry is listed as failed, and the next sync posts it
errorCases.userImpact: The feedback reaches the issue on a later sync

errorCases.scenario: The comment list needed to reconcile an uncertain post cannot be read
errorCases.detection: listComments fails before an unreceipted entry is posted
errorCases.response: That entry is not posted: an uncertain post is never retried blind
errorCases.userImpact: The entry waits for a sync that can read the issue

errorCases.scenario: A tracker comment's id was already recorded with different content
errorCases.detection: FeedbackService.add refuses the id as already used with different content
errorCases.response: The comment is listed as failed with that reason and the existing entry stands; nothing is overwritten
errorCases.userImpact: An edit made on the tracker after it was recorded is not mirrored

errorCases.scenario: A comment has an author that cannot be an actor id (an empty login, a deleted user)
errorCases.detection: The login is empty or does not make a namespaced lower-case id
errorCases.response: The comment is recorded under the actor github:unknown with the source kept, not dropped
errorCases.userImpact: The text is kept and its origin is traceable through the source

errorCases.scenario: The unit has no artifact, no binding or no tracker
errorCases.detection: The artifact id cannot be found, readBinding answers undefined, or openTracker answers a skip
errorCases.response: The sync does nothing and the result says why
errorCases.userImpact: A unit with no issue has nothing to read or post

invariantsToPreserve.text: Feedback entries are immutable and append-only: a recorded tracker comment is never changed or removed, and an edit or deletion on the tracker is never mirrored

No revision and no status of any artifact moves for a feedback entry or a receipt

migration.stateBefore: Comments on an issue are read only by the s6 attach and approve-time reconciliations; nothing records a human comment as feedback. FeedbackService.add writes feedback with no source, IssueOps.comment posts without answering an id, and the attach comment carries no marker (src/workflow/feedback/feedback-service.ts, src/workflow/tracker/github-adapter.ts, src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts). The build step's implement and validate phases do not touch the tracker for comments.
migration.stateAfter: A comment sync records human comments as feedback and posts locally entered feedback once, run from the build step's implement and validate phases and from the daemon method tracker.syncComments. FeedbackInput carries a source, the port has postComment, the attach comment carries a marker, and posts are recorded by revision-less receipts on the artifact's log.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional source to FeedbackInput and store it; no existing caller passes it, so stored feedback is unchanged

migration.backwardCompat: The new FeedbackInput source, the port's postComment and the marker line on attach comments are additive. Attach comments posted before this Story have no marker; isFrameworkComment recognises their shape, and s6's reconciliation of an attachment is by its link, which the new comment keeps. Nothing already stored is rewritten.

alternativesConsidered.name: One comment-sync module, called where the holder works, with receipts in the artifact's own log
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A single module reads human comments into feedback and posts unposted feedback, run from the build step's implement and validate phases and from a daemon method; once-only comes from entry ids and revision-less log receipts.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new src/workflow/tracker/comment-sync.ts holds syncUnitComments. Inbound: it reads the unit's issue from its binding, lists comments since a point derived from the artifact's latest tracker-sourced feedback (less a margin, because an overlap is harmless), drops every comment the framework posted (a marker test plus the pre-marker 'Attached' shape), and records each remaining comment through FeedbackService.add with the entry id tracker:<comment id> (so a repeat records nothing), the tracker login as a github:<login> actor, a kind taken from the first line (/revise or revision: gives revision-request, /suggest or suggestion: gives suggestion, anything else comment) and a source of { system: github, externalId, url }. Outbound: for each entry of the artifact that came from a person here (no source) and has no receipt, it looks for a comment carrying the entry's marker <!-- insrc:feedback:<artifactId>:<feedbackId> -->, posts one if none is found (through a new TrackerPort.postComment that returns the comment id), and appends a revision-less log entry on the artifact as the durable receipt (operation update, outcome posted, data kind feedback-post with feedbackId, externalId, issue). A tracker edit or deletion is never read back: a stored line is immutable and a recorded comment id is never revisited. The sync runs best-effort in the build step's implement and validate phases for the Task, and on request through a daemon method tracker.syncComments; a failure is returned in the result and never fails the phase. FeedbackInput gains an optional source (additive, s5's service).
pros: One owner for both directions, so the own-post filter and the once-only rules sit together
No new storage shape: the entry id, the existing sidecar dedup and a revision-less log entry (the pattern s7 used for build rounds) are enough
Reads happen only where the holder works on the unit, so there is no polling and no new credential
A crash after a post and before its receipt is repaired by the marker reconciliation, as the HLD's binding requirement 4 asks
cons: Touches the s5 feedback service (a source field) and the s6 port (postComment) additively, outside this Story's own files
The since point is derived and approximate; correctness rests on the idempotent entry id, not on the point

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the sync cursor and the receipts on the tracker binding
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The binding gains a comments block with the last read time and the posted receipts.
alternativesConsidered.approach: TrackerBinding gets a comments field: lastReadAt and posted receipts keyed by feedback id. The sync reads and patches the binding with the same synchronous meta-only patch s6 uses, instead of the artifact's log.
pros: The cursor is exact and the receipts sit beside the other tracker bookkeeping
cons: Changes the binding shape that s6 owns and the s9 conversion reads
The binding patch is a read-modify-write with a lost-update window; a lost receipt can post twice, which the log-based receipt does not risk
A receipt is not a change log fact, so it is not part of the artifact's history
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Exact cursor, but it changes s6's binding shape and risks a double post on a lost patch.

alternativesConsidered.name: A background poller for every bound issue
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A daemon loop reads comments for every open unit on an interval.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The daemon runs a timer that lists comments for each bound open issue and records them.
pros: Feedback is already there when the holder starts work
cons: Violates the Story's requirement: reading needs no background polling
Spends gh calls on units nobody is working on and has to pace itself against rate limits
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates the Story's no-polling requirement and spends calls on units nobody works on.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read comments on request only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Only the daemon method reads comments; implement and validate do not.
alternativesConsidered.approach: tracker.syncComments is the single entry; the build phases are left alone.
pros: Smallest: no change to the build step
cons: Fails ac24: the holder who starts to implement or validate is not given the comments unless they remember to ask
Outbound posting still needs its own trigger

openQuestions: FeedbackInput gets an optional source field, which is a change to the s5 feedback service (src/workflow/feedback/feedback-service.ts). Resolve: accept it as an additive s8-owned change (recommended), or record a tracker comment's origin only in its entry id and text (no source on the entry).

TrackerPort gains postComment so a post answers its comment id, an additive method on the sc6 port s6 owns. Resolve: accept it as additive with no HLD amendment (recommended), or file a sharedContract.methodAdd amendment on sc6 first.

The attach comment gets a marker line so the framework's own comments are told by a marker. This changes the text s6's attach posts, though not its link. Resolve: accept (recommended), or keep the attach comment as it is and recognise it only by its shape.

The comment commands are /revise and revision: for a revision request, /suggest and suggestion: for a suggestion, on the first line only. Resolve: accept these forms (recommended), or name other words.

A Story's comments are recorded on the artifact that holds its binding, the LLD, until s9 gives the Story its own artifact. Resolve: accept and record the move for s9 in docs/plans/core-data-model.md (recommended), or record Story comments only once the Story artifact exists.
